correctness.rationale: For every \(r\ge2,a\ge0,q\ge1\), the consecutive sampled observation row vectors are identified as \(1,H,H^2,\ldots\) in \(\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^n-1)\) with \(H=(1+X)^q\). CRT over F₂^r gives root 1 with factor \(Y^{\lceil 2^a/q\rceil}\), and each of h distinct nonzero eigenvalues with exponent \(2^{\max(a-v_2(q),0)}\). The multiplicities follow by an explicit w-adic leading-term calculation (q odd part nonzero), and h follows exactly from the gcd-kernel of the power map on F₂^r× after excluding 1. The minimal-polynomial degree proves first-row independence, saturated rank and nullity. The reconstructibility iff follows by strict comparison with \(n\). The standalone independent bit-vector rank code was executed and matched on 528 grid and 216 random cases; these tests only corroborate the unbounded proof.

value.rationale: Exactly quantifies how many initial bits a single stationary sensor can recover from temporally thinned observations, in an infinite and natural family of additive cellular-automaton rings; this is a motivated inverse dynamics problem. The formula distinguishes Frobenius spectral aliasing and the zero-mode nilpotent loss, and gives the sharp nontrivial obstruction: every \(q>1\) fails full recovery on even Mersenne-multiple rings. This is a symbolic structural theorem, not a generic observability-matrix recomputation, arbitrary finite cutoff, or merely a special sample table.
